title: A seller's website link runs code when clicked
brief: This code already uses textContent, so it looks like it has learned its lesson. A marketplace seller set their website to something that is not a website, and customers who click it lose their session. Text is not the only way into a page.
hints: textContent protected the name. The href is a different kind of sink: the browser does not render it, it navigates to it.
Blocking 'javascript:' means guessing every spelling an attacker might use. Which schemes does a seller's website actually need?
Parse it with new URL() and only set href when the protocol is 'https:' or 'http:'.
